notes:
EVIDENCE: build/h5reach/final/report.json.gz did not exist when I started; both it (written later) and the merged docs/harness5/redis-tcl-reach.json.gz have exactly the failing sets I triaged for list, stream and stream-cgroups in 2s/1s/Redis (checked). The finished final pass is split between build/h5reach/final-a/report.json.gz (2s + Redis) and build/h5reach/final-b/report.json.gz (1s). Both used the same union skip list and build/tomokv sha ef368a64..., the same binary as the full-file runs. Fresh --only reruns: build/b2-iso (cores 40-43, ports 45861/45862/45863, ratio 3:1, 2s/1s/Redis). Extra probes are under B2/work/probe*.json.

MODE DIFFERENCES ARE NOT MODE BUGS:
(1) In unit/type/list discovery, 2s gave 227/48 and 1s gave 240/35. The 13 extra 2s failures are the stale-client cascade of the flaky root 'BLMPOP with multiple blocked clients' (BLOCK-WAKE-ORDER-MULTI): it passed in 1s discovery attempt #3 and failed in 2s. In the final pass it failed in both modes, and both report the identical 48 failures.
(2) unit/type/zset (2s 4 failures, 1s 7) is the same mechanism. 'BZMPOP with multiple blocked clients' failed only in the 1s full-file run, but fails in fresh runs in both modes; #10762 and 'ZRANDMEMBER - listpack' are its cascades.
(3) Both wake-order roots are flaky in both modes: B2-BLOCK-WAKE-ORDER-MULTI was DIFFERENT in 4/6 runs (2s) and 5/6 (1s); the unpipelined chain probe in 5/6 (2s) and 2/6 (1s). A single SAME run does not mean fixed. The recorded B2-BLOCK-CHAIN-ASYNC case pipelines RPUSH+LRANGE and was DIFFERENT 4/4 in both modes.

CASCADE MECHANISM: a failing blocking test aborts with its deferring clients still blocked. Every later wait_for_blocked_clients_count is then off by the number of stale clients, and stale waiters steal elements pushed by later tests. Roots: list 'BLMPOP with multiple blocked clients', stream-cgroups 'Blocking XREADGROUP for stream key that has clients blocked on list' (missing total_blocking_keys), zset 'BZMPOP with multiple blocked clients'. Tests that also fail when run alone are classified by their own root with cascade_of null: Linked LMOVEs, Circular BRPOPLPUSH, both commandstats tests, the PAUSE test, both SORT..STORE tests, XGROUP DESTROY, and both RENAME/XREADGROUP tests.

HIDDEN HANGS: 'XGROUP DESTROY should unblock XREADGROUP with -NOGROUP', 'RENAME can unblock XREADGROUP with data' and 'RENAME can unblock XREADGROUP with -NOGROUP' hang when run alone, in both modes. In the reach pass the cascade made them fail fast. Once INFO-TOTAL-BLOCKING-KEYS is fixed, the stream-cgroups reach run will hang at XGROUP DESTROY unless these three join the skip list. Ten tests are hung in total: 3 list, 4 stream-cgroups on the skip list, plus these 3.

UNREACHED, NOT LISTED (block-level aborts with no test name; Redis runs these tests):
- unit/type/list: the first start_server block aborts at 'r config set list-compress-depth 2', skipping 6 '<packed|plain> node check compression ...' tests (quicklist compression, class-1 subject).
- unit/type/list-3: the 'foreach comp' block aborts at config_set list-compress-depth, skipping 5 tests (Stress tester for #3343-alike bugs comp: 0/1/2, and ziplist implementation: encoding stress testing / value encoding and backlink).
- unit/type/stream-cgroups: the needs:debug block at line 1074 with overrides {appendonly yes ...} aborts the rest of the file on the boot-only appendonly constraint, skipping 10 tests (XREADGROUP with NOACK creates consumer, Consumer without PEL is present in AOF after AOFRW, consumer-group lag/read-counter tests, legacy RDB loading, ...). The reach pass excluded needs:debug only for unit/type/stream (8 ignored there).

REDIS-SIDE REACH ARTIFACT: Redis fails 'BLMPOP_LEFT when result key is created by SORT..STORE' in the final pass ('no blocked clients') only because the skipped 'BLMPOP_LEFT when new key is moved into place' normally empties foo{t}. TomoKV fails the test independently (fresh run: SORT..STORE does not wake).

ISOLATION ARTIFACTS ON REDIS (not class 2):
- 'GETEX use of PERSIST option should remove TTL after loadaof': fails on Redis only in isolation (DEBUG LOADAOF right after enabling AOF); passes full-file.
- 'Consumer seen-time and active-time': --only fails on both servers because key x comes from an earlier test. The reach pass, where TomoKV fails at DUMP, is the evidence.
- 'Blocking timeout following PAUSE should honor the timeout': failed on Redis inside one multi-test --only batch but passes alone and in the full reach pass.

BRIEF CORRECTION: DEBUG OBJECT is NOT implemented on this base ('DEBUG OBJECT nokey' gives the unknown-subcommand error). Implemented: SET-ACTIVE-EXPIRE, LOADAOF, RELOAD, SLEEP (IoLoop), plus TomoKV-internal hooks.

JUDGEMENT CALLS (maintainer may override):
- MIGRATE-ABSENT is class 1: COMMAND LIST shows MIGRATE missing together with cluster*, module*, psync, replconf and sync.
- SRANDMEMBER long chain is class 2: it needs to own the server process (get_child_pid) and fails on Redis too. Its 6 SMOVE cascades fail identically on Redis.
- STREAM-TRIM-APPROX-LIMIT is REAL, not class 1: LIMIT is a documented eviction cap, and TomoKV does have nodes (stream-node-max-entries is honoured for node rolling).
- DIRTY-COUNTER is class 2 (persistence-internal counter), but even with save points armed TomoKV miscounts a served BLPOP (+3 vs +2) and XREADGROUP (+0 vs +2).
- No defect is hidden behind the class-1 failures that I checked: COPY of list/set/zset/hash/stream (with a group and PEL) and RESTORE ABSTTL-in-the-past match Redis exactly.

REPRO NOTES:
- B2-INFO-TOTAL-BLOCKING-KEYS and B2-PAUSE-POSTPONED-NOT-BLOCKED compare the whole INFO clients text, so DIFFERENT also reflects fields TomoKV never prints. The defining field is named in each root.
- B2-INFO-CMDSTAT-FIELDS is SAME by construction (Redis usec values are volatile, so compare:false); use the upstream --only selection named in its design_note.
- B2-RESTORE-IDLETIME-FREQ-IGNORED uses an all-ASCII DUMP payload for the string 'v26' (RDB v12 + Redis CRC64), because repro_tcl.py sends UTF-8 text.

HARNESS: Redis's find_available_port also binds port+10000 (55862 here). One isolation batch hit "Can't find a non busy port in the 45862-45862 range" transiently; my runner now retries.

INTEGRATION (lead): the four block-setup failures above (list, list-3, stream, stream-cgroups) were listed in notes rather than tests; they are now explicit entries with test name <file setup/teardown>.
